title: The Weaver's Altar of Yarn
story:
James left Lookout Bridge behind as the morning mist burned off the cobblestones, following the winding alleys until he smelled the familiar scent of woodsmoke and wool. James had never seen such quiet industriousness in the early hours; James had never felt such comforting warmth radiating from a single doorway; James had never known a human town could feel so much like a second home. He pushed open the heavy wooden door to Mateo's workshop, slipping quietly inside just as the weaver was settling into his massive wooden loom. Mateo looked up from his shuttles, a familiar, weathered smile breaking across his face as he recognized the small visitor.

Mateo gestured toward the glowing hearth where a fresh pot of herbal tea sat steaming alongside a basket of soft, honey-drizzled bread. James pulled his weathered leather strap a bit tighter, letting his green sea-glass dangle against his chest before climbing up onto a high wooden stool near the loom. They shared a quiet, companionable breakfast in the rhythmic clack-clack of the shuttle, the motion hypnotic and steady against the hum of awakening Oakhaven outside. Mateo showed James how the colorful threads were dyed using crushed mountain flowers and roots, pressing a small spool of deep indigo wool directly into James's waiting palm as a token of their growing friendship.

As the afternoon sun cast long golden beams across the workshop floor, James took out his brass map canister and carefully unwound his leather strap to re-tie the new indigo thread right beside Mateo's earlier colorful braids. The threads felt like a growing tapestry of his journey, a physical reminder of every hand that had offered him kindness since he left the Great Canopy. He traced the smooth metal of his single brass coin with one thumb, wondering where the winding streets might lead him next once the shadows lengthened over the Plaza of the Fountain.

With a final nod to the weaver, James stepped back out into the cool evening air of Oakhaven, the indigo thread glowing softly against his worn leather gear. He paused at the edge of the canal to watch the flat-bottomed barges drift past under the evening stars, whispering his quiet greeting to the dark water and whatever adventures waited around the next bend.
